title: Oath of Flame & Light
subtitle: Dawn & Vows

lore.description:
There is a kind of person who cannot bear to be doubted, and a kind who cannot bear to have doubted themselves. The Oath takes both.

It is not a god and has never claimed to be. It is what happens when a promise is spoken aloud, in front of witnesses, in the first light — the moment the words stop belonging to you and become a thing in the world that other people are entitled to hold you to. The fire is only the visible part of it.

To swear in it is to give up the ordinary mercies: the second thought, the quiet revision, the kinder version of the story told afterward. The sworn stand where they can be seen. That is the whole discipline. The smiting, the healing, the light that finds a lie in a crowded room — all of it comes out of that, and not the other way around.
lore.followers: The Oath answers to many names and does not appear to mind which. It is called on most by the magic-workers of the Church of Flame and the Temple of Light, though any faith that keeps a fire keeps some part of it. What its people share is not doctrine. It is a particular restlessness — the condition of having said a thing out loud and now having to be the person who said it, every morning, in front of everyone.

names_across_regions.everflame: The Everflame — the unquenchable fire of promise, carried from shrine to shrine by wandering priests of the Church of Flame. Its censers never cool.
names_across_regions.aeler: Adur, the Light of Aeler — worshiped as the sun's church-deity, whose flame consecrates oaths and consumes falsehood. Dwarven templars strike their oaths into stone with a brand.
names_across_regions.vilikari: Adar, the Vilikari Dawnfire — invoked as a war-god of vows and vengeance, whose rising light marks those who break faith. Cavalrymen light a single arrow before battle.
names_across_regions.vhasia: The Watchfire of Vhasia — a saint's flame that never gutters, tended by a silent order of healers who swear to harm no one — and to let no one die alone.

lore.quote: Say it where they can hear you. After that it is not yours to soften.

domain_focus: Sacred Vows: oath-keeping, truth-speaking, binding promises
Divine Justice: retribution, smiting evil, protecting the innocent
Radiant Power: healing light, purification, revealing truth
Dawn's Hope: renewal, protection, driving back darkness

thiasos.description: What comes to a sworn of the Oath comes at sunrise and expects to be sworn in front of. A salamander the color of a coal that has been fed. A brass-scaled lizard that warms in the hand when a vow is true and cools when the wording is not. A golden-eyed owl that calls only at dawn. A phoenix fledgling barely a handful across, which will not go out.
thiasos.care: It does not eat. It must be present when the day's vows are renewed at first light. Neglected a week its glow gutters and fails, and it is Compromised (–1 die on social rolls involving oaths or truth for its bearer) until a new vow is sworn where it can see.

codex.description: The Oath's Rites are not kept in ink. A brass scroll whose letters rise when the words are read aloud. Nine candles, each flame standing for a clause. A sun-stone that shows nothing at all indoors and will not be argued with about it.
codex.upkeep: Light is a poor archivist. An hour each week in dawn light with every Rite read aloud, or the engravings sink back into the metal (treat as Compromised until re-consecrated at first light).

patrons_gift.name: Oath's Blessing
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of the Oath of Flame & Light may touch a held item (weapon, shield, or badge) and whisper a vow of protection.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Defend or Resist rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would be forced to break a sworn oath by magical compulsion, they may ignore it (the flame burns through the coercion).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to the Oath of Flame & Light.

rites.name: Rite of Kindle Vow
rites.materials: A glass ampoule of consecrated flame, broken in the open where people are watching.
rites.effect: Declare a short vow for this scene (e.g., 'protect the villagers,' 'speak only truth'). The bearer gains +1 die to actions fulfilling it.
rites.push_it: The first hesitation forces 1 SB (Hearts) on the bearer. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Lay on Hands
rites.materials: A bare palm and a vow said close enough to be heard by the one you are touching.
rites.effect: Cleanse an affliction, downgrade Harm by 1, or remove 1 Fatigue. For curses or poisons, test Spirit+Resolve (DV set by fiction).
rites.push_it: The target gains +1 die to their next Resist roll this scene; you mark Exposure +1. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Sunlit Parley
rites.materials: A vow-ring cut with a sunrise, turned so the table can see it.
rites.effect: Establish terms in open light. Honest persuasion gains +1 die; deceit suffers –1 die. Create a 6-segment Parley Accord timer.
rites.push_it: Demand one public answer; evasion forces 1 SB (Hearts) on the evader. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Radiant Smite
rites.materials: A consecrated spark set into a weapon or a badge of office.
rites.effect: Your next melee strike flares with dawnfire. Upgrade Effect by one step, add +1 Burn Harm, or impose –1 die on the target's next roll. Against undead, oath-breakers, or outsiders: oath-breakers suffer +1 Harm and –1 die; outsiders gain +1 leash ticks.
rites.push_it: The attack ignores the target's armor entirely (no armor conversion applies to this strike; the target marks direct Harm). Additionally, the burst drives back enemies in Close (worse Position). Mark +1 additional Obligation (total +3). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Purge the Shadow
rites.materials: A consecrated spark, shattered on purpose.
rites.effect: Reveal illusions and suppress one ongoing glamour or curse in Near range. Creates a 4-segment Purity's Light timer.
rites.push_it: Brand the source with a visible tell for this arc; mark 1 SB (Diamonds). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Covenant Blaze
rites.materials: A brazier lit while three names are spoken by three separate voices.
rites.effect: The sworn within are haloed: they gain +1 die to keep their oath; aggressors suffer –1 die if violating the terms. Oath-breakers suffer 2 SB (Hearts/Spades) and Harm 1 (Burn).
rites.push_it: Sanctify a threshold with one beat of [WARD] against oath-breakers; mark +2 Obligation. Cost: Mark +2 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of the Oath sings clear and high — a trumpet at sunrise, a bell over a valley that has not woken up yet. The voice is used to swear a witness in, to consecrate a blade in a single held note, to turn a funeral pyre into something a lost column can steer by. You find them in marching camps and on pilgrim roads, keeping vows warm in men who would otherwise have talked themselves out of them by the second week.

cult.name: The Cult of the Unquenched Flame
cult.description: They gather at dawn, in open courtyards or on hilltops facing east, because the point is to be visible. The Unquenched Flame is a fellowship of paladins, healers, and ordinary people who have agreed to keep one another honest, which is harder work than any of the fighting. Each speaks a vow as the sun clears the horizon and passes a lit candle on; the flame must reach the last speaker alive. Their creed is written in charcoal over every hearth they keep. Outsiders are welcome to swear something small and share the light, and are told plainly beforehand that a vow made at dawn holds until sunset.

witchcraft.name: The Ascetic's Art
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with the Oath is often a consecrated scribe, a censer-bearer, or a vowed healer — a nun, monk, or scholar of one of the great flame-temples. Their magic is inseparable from liturgy, prayer, and the careful tending of sacred spaces. They illuminate manuscripts with gold leaf that glows in the presence of lies, brew unguents from ashes of the everflame, and copy oath-books whose letters burn when a vow is broken. In Aeler, a True-Mason might carve a 'prayer keystone' into a basilica wall, so that every confession spoken there warms the stone. In Vhasia, a silent sister might stitch a healing shroud that records the wounds it has mended. These ascetics live alongside their monastic brethren in abbeys, monasteries, and convents, their craft a form of prayer made manifest.
witchcraft.lore: The ascetic's path is devotion made visible. Every working is a prayer, every healing a sacrament, every vow a fire that somebody has to get up and tend. The Oath's witches do not chase power; they chase exactness of purpose, and the light comes into them sideways while they are busy with the work. None of it is spectacular. It is the scriptorium, the infirmary, the chapel at four in the morning, and someone still awake in it.
witchcraft.quote: The flame that reveals the truth also warms the hands that keep it.

prayer_beads.name: Prayer Beads of the Unbroken Vow
prayer_beads.description: A string of nine beads carved from olive wood and fired in a basilica's censer. Each bead represents a clause of a sacred oath. Once per session, the witch may slip the beads around a door handle, a prisoner's wrist, or a contract scroll. While the beads remain, any creature that knowingly violates an oath sworn under that threshold suffers a mild burn (1 Fatigue) as the beads glow faintly. The beads may also be used to count a silent vow; the witch may reroll one failed Resolve roll when upholding that vow.

hedge_gifts.name: Sealed Benediction
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may lay a hand on a willing creature's forehead and speak a short, formal blessing (e.g., 'May the flame keep your word'). The target gains +1 die on their next roll to resist fear, despair, or magical coercion. The blessing lasts until the next dawn. The witch must write the blessing on a scrap of parchment and burn it; the smoke carries the prayer.

hedge_gifts.name: Censer's Blessing
hedge_gifts.description: You may swing a censer (or any vessel that holds smoke) to fill a Near zone with cleansing incense. For the next scene, any supernatural creature within the zone suffers –1 die to all rolls, and any magical effect passing through the smoke is treated as one Tier lower for resistance. The censer can also be used to 'cense' a threshold: sprinkling ash from the censer across a doorway applies a [WARD] tag against minor spirits and undead until the next dawn.

hedge_gifts.name: Dawnfire Reading
hedge_gifts.description: When you hold a piece of parchment or a book up to dawn light, you may ask the GM one yes/no question about whether the text contains a lie, a broken oath, or a false promise. The parchment glows faintly if the answer is 'yes.' Once per scene.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Unquenched Flame
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Unquenched Flame live by the vow and the dawn. They are paladins and scribes, healers and judges, and they take the last of those most seriously. Their bodies are the temple, their word is the fire, and their fists come down like a verdict already read aloud. They keep the same vigils as their witch brethren in the same abbeys, and the two orders argue constantly about everything except what they got up for.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Spirit 3+, Body 2+, Rite of Kindle Vow or Cantor of the Oath.
monastic_tradition.quote: Say it where they can hear you. After that it is not yours to soften.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Oath does not forget, but it does hold with those who keep the flame. Monks of the Unquenched Flame gain +1 die to resist any binding, geas, or compulsion that would force them to break a sworn oath or take shelter in a lie. On a success the compulsion burns off like mist and the vow stands where it was, in the open, where everyone can see it did not move.

basic.name: Sworn Defender
basic.description: When you take the Defend action, you may also grant an adjacent ally +1 Armor until your next turn. The flame protects those who stand beside you.

advanced.name: Radiant Resolve
advanced.description: Once per scene when you would be affected by fear, despair, or magical coercion, you may instead ignore the effect entirely. The flame burns through the darkness, and you stand unshaken.

master.name: Avatar of the Oath
master.description: Once per session, you may become a living covenant for one scene. You gain +2 dice to all protection, justice, and oath-keeping actions. Additionally, any creature that breaks a sworn oath in your presence suffers 2 SB (Hearts/Spades) and Harm 1 (Burn) as the flame demands account.
master.cost: 2 Fatigue and +1 Obligation to the Oath

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Oathbound Strength: +1 die when upholding vows or defending innocents.
corruption.cost: Rigid Honor: Must uphold vows even when disadvantageous; –1 die to flexible actions.

corruption.benefit: Radiant Sight: Once/scene, +2 dice to detect lies or corruption.
corruption.cost: Blinding Truth: –1 die to subtlety or deception attempts.

corruption.benefit: Holy Flame: +1 die to melee against undead, outsiders, or oath-breakers.
corruption.cost: Burden of Light: 1 Fatigue when concealing identity or working in darkness.

corruption.benefit: Unwavering Resolve: Once/session, treat a failed Resolve/Command as success (mark 1 SB).
corruption.cost: Absolutist Stance: –1 die in morally ambiguous situations.

corruption.benefit: Dawn's Benediction: Once/session, heal all allies in Near of 1 Fatigue and minor Conditions.
corruption.cost: Beacon's Call: Your aura reveals you; enemies seeking you gain +1 die.

corruption.benefit: Avatar of the Oath: Once/session, become a living covenant (+2 dice to protection/justice actions).
corruption.cost: Radiance's Price: Mark +2 Obligation; breaking any vow inflicts Harm 2 (Burn).

playstyle_notes.description: The Oath is the patron for a character who has decided something and would rather be broken than revised. It gives hard defense, clean healing, and a light that makes deceit expensive, and it charges for all of it in flexibility: the sworn cannot slip a room, cannot walk back a promise made in haste, and cannot be quietly wrong. Its corruption does not turn a character cruel. It turns them certain, which at the table is often worse and always more interesting.
emphasizes: Said out loud — vows that are binding because witnesses heard them, not because magic did
No shadow to stand in — the sworn are visible, and visibility is the cost and the weapon
Judgment before violence — the smiting is a verdict; the verdict came first
Light as an inconvenience — truth surfacing at the least convenient hour, including your own
Certainty as the corruption — the slow narrowing of a person who is never allowed to be unsure

sample_adventure.title: The Oath That Binds
sample_adventure.description: A knight of the Unquenched Flame swore to hold a village and rode out when the raiders came. The village burned. The survivors have walked four days to ask for her, and they are not asking politely. She says a shadow-touched relic took her, and she may believe it. The relic is real and the party can find it, and what they will not be able to find is anyone at the abbey willing to say out loud whether that changes anything.
sample_adventure.quote: She says the thing took her. Perhaps it did. She still has to stand in the light and say what she did, and so do the rest of us who let her ride out alone.
